project_type: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Framer Motion + GSAP image-sequence scrolling website
test_framework: No test framework configured - verification is build + runtime behavior
verification_instructions: 1. Run npm run build and confirm zero errors. 2. Verify that public/*-vdo/ directories contain only 150 WebP files each (odd-numbered frames converted). 3. Verify src/hooks/useSequencesPreload.ts only loads 1st-vdo as critical. 4. Verify FRAME_COUNT is 150 in HomeExperience.tsx.
snapshot_or_generated_files: public/1st-vdo/, public/2nd-vdo/, public/3rd-vdo/, public/4th-vdo/ - image frames generated by conversion script. Also public/1st-vdo-thumb/, etc. for thumbnails.
setup_instructions: npm install (already done). sharp devDependency already installed.
environment_constraints: Network available (sharp installed). Pillow installed via pip3. Node v22. No cwebp CLI but sharp is available for WebP conversion.
key_patterns: Image sequences loaded by useSequencesPreload hook into imagesRef (Record<string, HTMLImageElement[]>). ImageSequencePlayer draws frames imperatively via drawFrame(index). Hero uses 1st-vdo, 2nd-vdo, 3rd-vdo with scroll-tied animation. ReservationMotionSection and ContactSection use 4th-vdo. HomeExperience defines FRAME_COUNT and passes to all components.
directory_structure: src/components/ - React components. src/hooks/ - custom hooks. src/lib/story/ - scroll math. public/1st-vdo..4th-vdo/ - 300 JPG frames each at 1920x1080. Each frame ~140-180KB.
